children: The near-term impact of the EU's deal with China to halve the latter's exports of hybrids to the EU for the next four years is modestly negative but manageable, say Bernstein analysts in a note. In the longer term, the impact should be largely neutral as major Chinese automakers are already localizing production in Europe, with BYD set to start production in Hungary by end-2026. Leapmotor is leveraging Stellantis's manufacturing footprint in Spain, and Geely is targeting production at Ford's Spain plant from 2028, Bernstein adds. It doesn't expect the measures to materially derail market-share gains by Chinese automakers beyond an initial adjustment period, similar to EU tariffs on full EVs. The key question is whether automakers can preserve unit economics as production localizes, Bernstein says. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
